context: You've got off the bus in a small town and need to find your guesthouse. Today: asking the way, understanding the answer, and where to go when you're really lost.

phrases.jp: すみません、{駅|えき}はどちらですか。
phrases.en: Excuse me, which way is the station?
phrases.note: どちら is a politer どこ. Perfect for strangers.

phrases.jp: ここから{歩|ある}いて{行|い}けますか。
phrases.en: Can I walk there from here?

phrases.jp: {地図|ちず}で{教|おし}えてもらえますか。
phrases.en: Could you show me on the map?
phrases.note: Hold out your phone map while you say it. Much easier for both of you.

phrases.jp: この{道|みち}をまっすぐ{行|い}って、{二|ふた}つ{目|め}の{信号|しんごう}を{右|みぎ}です。
phrases.en: Go straight down this road and turn right at the second traffic light.
phrases.note: This is what you'll HEAR. Listen for the ～て chain: {行|い}って → then the turn.

phrases.jp: コンビニの{角|かど}を{曲|ま}がるんだよね？
phrases.en: We turn at the corner with the konbini, right?
phrases.note: ～んだよね？ checks something you think is true. Great with friends.

dialogue_setting: On a quiet street in a mountain town, asking an older local.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: すみません、「やまびこ」っていうゲストハウスを{探|さが}しているんですが…
dialogue.en: Excuse me, I'm looking for a guesthouse called Yamabiko…

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.jp: ああ、やまびこね。この{道|みち}をまっすぐ{行|い}って、{橋|はし}を{渡|わた}ったら{左|ひだり}だよ。
dialogue.en: Ah, Yamabiko. Go straight along this road, and after you cross the bridge it's on the left.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {橋|はし}を{渡|わた}って{左|ひだり}ですね。{歩|ある}いて{何分|なんぷん}ぐらいですか。
dialogue.en: Cross the bridge, then left. About how many minutes on foot?

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.jp: うーん、10{分|ぷん}ぐらいかな。{坂|さか}がちょっときついけどね。
dialogue.en: Hmm, about 10 minutes. The slope is a bit steep, though.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: わかりました。ありがとうございます！
dialogue.en: Got it. Thank you very much!

kanji.where: Small police posts near stations and big crossings. Officers there give directions all day and have detailed local maps, so it's the best place to go when you're really lost.
kanji.related: Related: {案内所|あんないじょ} information desk, {観光案内所|かんこうあんないじょ} tourist information.

tip.title: Streets don't have names
tip.body: Most Japanese streets have no names, and addresses go by district, block and building number. So people give directions by landmarks: konbini, traffic lights ({信号|しんごう}), bridges. Learn {角|かど} (corner), {突|つ}き{当|あ}たり (end of the road) and {手前|てまえ} (just before). In the countryside someone may even walk you there, so thank them warmly.

challenge.prompt: You're lost near a station. Ask a passer-by: "Excuse me, is there a konbini around here?"
challenge.hint: around here = この{辺|へん}, is there…? = …はありますか
challenge.model_answer: すみません、この{辺|へん}にコンビニはありますか。
